text: Designing a good API is like creating a clear set of instructions for two programs to talk to each other. REST APIs are a popular way to do this, where you use simple endpoints (like URLs) to access data or actions. When building these, it is crucial to use proper HTTP status codes, such as 200 for success or 404 for not found, so that developers immediately understand what happened. Another key habit is to write clear, up-to-date documentation. Without it, even a perfect API is hard to use. Finally, always plan for versioning. You can include a version number in the URL, like `/v1/users`, so that when you make changes, old users are not broken. Following these simple rules makes life much easier for everyone.
